stem: How much org-wide Apex code coverage is required to deploy to production?
explanation: The org needs at least 75% coverage with all tests passing.

stem: Which statement about triggers and coverage is true?
explanation: Each trigger must have coverage above 0%.

stem: Which annotation marks a class or method as a test?
explanation: @isTest marks a class or method as test code. Test code is not counted against the org's Apex size limit and its data is rolled back when the test ends.

stem: Is test data saved to the database after tests run?
explanation: Records created in tests are rolled back.

stem: By default, can test methods see existing org data?
explanation: Tests do not see the org's existing records unless SeeAllData=true is set, which is discouraged. Create your own data so the test works in any org.

stem: What does Test.startTest() do?

options.text: Starts a fresh set of governor limits for the code under test
Starts the database transaction that is rolled back when the test ends
Deletes all of the data that the test class created earlier on
Turns on debug logs for every user while the test method runs

explanation: startTest and stopTest give the code in between its own limits.

stem: What does Test.stopTest() do with asynchronous jobs?

options.text: Cancels them so that nothing runs after the test ends
Ignores them so the test finishes more quickly
Queues them for tomorrow so they run outside the test

explanation: Async work finishes at stopTest so assertions can run.

stem: Why is a test with no assertions weak?

options.text: It may cover lines but does not prove behaviour
It fails deployment because Salesforce rejects empty tests
It takes longer to run than a test that has assertions
It deletes the data that the method created during setup

explanation: Coverage is not the same as correctness.

stem: Which assertion method checks that two values match?
explanation: System.assertEquals and Assert.areEqual compare expected and actual.

stem: Which annotation creates shared test data once for all methods in the class?
explanation: @testSetup runs once before test methods.

stem: Which method tests code as a different user?
explanation: runAs applies that user's permissions and sharing.

stem: How do you test code that makes an HTTP callout?

options.text: Call the real endpoint during the test so the result is genuine
Skip the callout code and rely on manual testing
Use SeeAllData so the test can reach the endpoint

explanation: Tests are not allowed to make real callouts. Use Test.setMock with a class that implements HttpCalloutMock so the test gets a controlled fake response.

stem: What is the best number of records to use in a bulk trigger test?
explanation: A trigger receives records in batches of up to 200, so inserting 200 records in one DML shows whether your code is bulk-safe. One record hides SOQL and DML in loops.

stem: What is a test data factory?

options.text: A utility class that creates test records
A flow that creates test records when a user saves
A trigger that inserts sample data into production
A permission set that lets tests see all org data

explanation: A factory centralises test record creation.

stem: Can test classes count towards the org's Apex code size limit?
explanation: Test classes marked @isTest are excluded.

stem: A developer needs the test to load records from a CSV static resource. Which method?
explanation: Test.loadData loads records from a static resource.

stem: What must happen during deployment to production for tests?

options.text: Apex tests run and must all pass

explanation: Production deployments with Apex run local tests by default and all must pass.

stem: Why do tests need their own data?

options.text: Org data may differ between sandbox and production
Org data is hidden by the platform in all cases

explanation: Dependence on org data makes tests fragile.

stem: Which TWO are good test cases for a trigger? (Choose 2)

options.text: A negative case that expects an error
A test using real customer records

explanation: Good trigger tests cover a bulk run of 200 records and a negative case that expects an error. A test with no assertions, or one that relies on real customer data, proves nothing.

stem: A test for a flow-triggered process fails because a flow also updates the field. What should the developer remember?

options.text: Record-triggered flows also run during tests
Flows never run in tests, so the flow cannot be the cause
Flows run only in production, and not in a sandbox or test
Flows run after the test ends, so they cannot change the field

explanation: Declarative automation runs on test DML, so expectations must include it.

It fails because 502 accounts exist in the org
It fails because tests need SeeAllData to run
It passes only in a sandbox, not in production

explanation: Test methods start with an empty data set unless SeeAllData=true, so only the two inserted records are counted.

options.text: Wrap the enqueue in Test.startTest() and Test.stopTest()
Add SeeAllData=true to the test class so the job can see org data
Replace the queueable job with a future method and keep the assertion
Delete the assertion because asynchronous work cannot be checked in a test

explanation: Asynchronous work runs only when stopTest is called, so the assertion must come after Test.stopTest().

stem: Which TWO statements about test data are true? (Choose 2)

options.text: Records created by a test are rolled back when it ends
Test code can use @testSetup to create shared data once
Tests should depend on existing production records
Test data counts toward storage limits permanently

explanation: Test data is temporary and @testSetup shares setup across methods. Depending on org data makes tests fragile.
